summary: EU27 plus UK average VSL of about EUR 4.7M (2024 prices, ~USD 5.1M at ~1.08 EUR/USD) from the 2016 EC DG-MOVE study - a regional reference for European income-to-WTP calibration, not a single jurisdiction.
source_citation: European Commission DG MOVE (2016), via EUROCONTROL Standard Inputs (ansperformance.eu).

summary: Greece stated-preference human cost per road fatality of about USD 1.6M (2024, from ~$1.0M 2004 USD; ~EUR 816,500), paired with GDP/capita ~USD 29,700; Greece consistently ranks among low-VSL EU states given lower income.
label_raw: human cost per road fatality ~EUR 816,500 (~$1.0M, 2004 USD)
source_citation: Salata & Androulidakis (NTUA, 2004), via Yannis NRSO; broader Greek SP work Yannis et al., European Transport Research Review (2013), s12544-013-0103-3.

summary: Israel has no published citable national VSL located; an income-transfer-implied VSL of roughly USD 7-9M (2024) at GDP/capita ~USD 69,800 is explicitly UNVERIFIED and recorded only as a flagged gap, so no money value is asserted.
label_raw: no published national VSL; implied ~$7-9M (UNVERIFIED), GDP/capita ~$69,800
source_citation: No retrievable Israeli Ministry of Transport / road-safety CBA VSL; implied figure derived from Viscusi-type income elasticity only (flagged gap).

summary: Italy Becker health-demand income-transfer VSL of about USD 4.6M (2024, from $3.8M 2020 USD x1.22; gamma=0.5, r=5%, revealed/WTP hybrid anchored to income), paired with GDP/capita rising from $34,460 (2020) to ~$46,500 (2024-25).
source_citation: Revisiting the value of a statistical life: an international approach during COVID-19, Risk Management (2022), PMC9017085, Table 1; corroboration Alberini & Scasny, Environmental & Resource Economics 49(4):511-538 (2011).

summary: Malaysia conjoint-analysis stated-preference VSL of about USD 0.65M (2024, from ~$0.45M 2010 USD x1.40; ~RM 1.45M car drivers), paired with GDP/capita ~USD 15,100; far below the Masterman-Viscusi income-transfer figure (~$3.1M), flagging large transfer-vs-local-WTP divergence.
source_citation: Ghani & Yusoff (MIROS), Malaysian Value of Statistical Life for Fatal Injury in Road Accident, ResearchGate 260991699.

summary: Malaysia Masterman-Viscusi income-transfer VSL of about USD 3.1M (2024, from 2013 VSL ~$2.3M 2015 USD x1.33), far above the domestic stated-preference figure (~$0.65M); large divergence flagged.
source_citation: Masterman & Viscusi (2018), income-transfer; Journal of Benefit-Cost Analysis 9(3):407-434.

summary: Norway official government cost-benefit VSL of about USD 4.1M (2024, from ~$3.8M 2022 USD; ~36M NOK, VSLY ~575,000 NOK), paired with very high oil-inflated GDP/capita ~USD 105,900 - a low implied income-elasticity anchor.
source_citation: Norwegian Ministry of Finance guidance, via Andersson-Treich handbook references and eleuven/vslcovid19 GitHub dataset.

summary: Poland Becker income-transfer VSL of about USD 2.1M (2024, from $1.7M 2020 USD x1.22), paired with GDP/capita rising from $15,200 (2020) to ~$31,300 (2024-25).
source_citation: Revisiting VSL international approach during COVID-19, Risk Management (2022), PMC9017085, Table 1.

summary: Poland revealed-preference (wage-risk) VSL of about USD 2.4M (2024, mid ~$1.6M 2008 USD x1.47; range $0.79-2.41M), paired with GDP/capita ~USD 31,300.
source_citation: Giergiczny (2008), Value of a Statistical Life - the Case of Poland, ResearchGate 5147115.

summary: South Korea contingent-valuation WTP VSL of roughly USD 0.9M (2024, from ~$0.7M 2014 USD; ~796M KRW/person) to avoid cancer mortality from carcinogenic chemicals, paired with GDP/capita ~USD 37,400; brackets the low end of the Korean SP range.
source_citation: Shin et al., Value of a statistical life estimation of carcinogenic chemicals in Korea, PMC4540128 (2015); GDP/capita IMF nominal.

summary: South Korea stated-preference WTP VSL of about USD 2.5M (2024, midpoint of $1.8-3.2M from $1.4-2.5M 2018 USD x1.26) for PM10/PM2.5 mortality-risk reduction via an air-purifier discrete-choice experiment, paired with GDP/capita ~USD 37,400.
source_citation: Lee et al., Journal of Environmental Management (2024), ScienceDirect S0301479724033930; GDP/capita IMF nominal (Wikipedia List of countries by GDP (nominal) per capita).

summary: Spain Becker income-transfer VSL of about USD 4.0M (2024, from $3.3M 2020 USD x1.22), paired with GDP/capita rising from $30,390 (2020) to ~$41,600 (2024-25); notably above the official Spanish stated-preference figure (~$2.1M).
source_citation: Revisiting VSL international approach during COVID-19, Risk Management (2022), PMC9017085, Table 1.

summary: Spain official road-safety stated-preference VSL of about USD 2.1M (2024; DGT ~EUR 1.9M, CV/standard-gamble range EUR 1.3-2.1M), paired with GDP/capita ~USD 41,600; below the income-transfer figure, illustrating transfer-over-states-local-WTP divergence (revealed-preference Spanish studies run EUR 2.8-8.3M).
source_citation: Direccion General de Trafico (DGT), Update of the monetary value of a statistical life in Spain (2025), dgt.es; Martin-Fernandez / Abellan-Perpinan lineage.

summary: Turkey Becker income-transfer VSL of about USD 1.3M (2024, from $1.1M 2020 USD x1.22) at GDP/capita $9,610 (2020), higher than the Turkish primary stated-preference estimate (~$0.67M); divergence flagged.
source_citation: Revisiting VSL international approach during COVID-19, Risk Management (2022), PMC9017085, Table 1.

summary: Turkey stated-preference choice-experiment VSL of about USD 0.67M (2024, from ~0.49M PPP USD 2012 x1.37; ~740,838 TL), paired with GDP/capita ~USD 19,000; well below the Becker-transfer estimate (~$1.3M), flagging transfer-over-states-WTP divergence.
source_citation: Tekesin & Ara, Measuring the Value of Mortality Risk Reductions in Turkey, PMC4113852 (2014).

summary: United States base VSL of about USD 12.8M (2024, from $9.6M 2015 USD x1.33), the anchor for stepped income elasticity (~1.0 below $2M VSL, ~0.55 above) used to scale VSL across jurisdictions.
source_citation: Masterman & Viscusi, The Income Elasticity of Global Values of a Statistical Life, Journal of Benefit-Cost Analysis 9(3):407-434 (2018), Cambridge Core.

summary: World Bank income-tier average VSLs (2015 USD): low $107k, lower-middle $420k, upper-middle $1.2M, high $6.4M (high tier ~$8.5M in 2024 USD x1.33) - a direct income-to-WTP calibration ladder for L_to_M normalization.
label_raw: World Bank income-tier average VSL (2015 USD): $107k / $420k / $1.2M / $6.4M
source_citation: Masterman & Viscusi, Journal of Benefit-Cost Analysis 9(3):407-434 (2018), Cambridge Core.
